opening: I am writing to apply for the AI software engineer role at EggAI. Your framing of the problem, helping large organisations move AI from prototype into production, is the gap I have spent three years working in from the other side, as the person actually shipping the thing rather than the person specifying it. Most AI work dies between the demo and the first week in front of real users, and the reason is almost never the model.
role_specific: The parts of your requirements I can speak to honestly are the production ones. At FlowSpace I built the support AI agents that ran against real users, dealt with latency and reliability, and built the fallback path for when a model returns something the next step cannot use. I have done prompt chaining, RAG retrieval over real document sets, function calling and structured outputs, and direct integration of OpenAI and Anthropic APIs into workflows that other systems depend on. For UltraStrategy I built a CV parsing tool in n8n with Eden AI; for Get2Germany, automated workflows with Google APIs. My languages are Python for parsing and integration work and TypeScript across Next.js and Laravel products, and I led a migration from Bubble.io to Next.js and Laravel on a live product while it grew from 2,000 to over 4,500 users.
closing: The gaps are real and I would rather name them than have you find them. I have not used Braintrust or Langfuse, and my evaluation practice has been hand-built regression checks rather than a proper eval suite with model-graded or reference-based metrics. I have not run formal prompt versioning or deployment pipelines. And the body of your posting says Senior Engineer while the stated bar is two years of core LLM engineering; I am at about three years with no CS degree, so if Senior is the real requirement I am not your candidate and I would rather say so. If the two-year bar is the real one, I would like to talk.
